verses.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by God's will, in keeping with the promise of life in Christ Jesus,
to Timothy, my dear child: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
I thank God, whom I serve as my ancestors did with a clear conscience. Night and day, I remember you in my prayers.
I long to see you. I remember your tears, and I would be filled with joy.
I remember your sincere faith, which first lived in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice, and I'm convinced it lives in you too.
That's why I remind you to fan into flame the gift of God that is in you through the laying on of my hands.
God didn't give us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.
So don't be ashamed of the testimony about our Lord or of me, his prisoner. Instead, share in suffering for the Good News by God's power.
God saved us and called us to a holy calling—not because of what we did, but because of his own purpose and grace. He gave us this grace in Christ Jesus before time began,
and now he has revealed it through the appearing of our Savior, Christ Jesus. He broke the power of death and brought life and immortality to light through the Good News.
I was appointed to serve as its preacher, apostle, and teacher to the Gentiles.
That's why I suffer as I do. But I'm not ashamed, because I know the one I've trusted, and I'm convinced he can guard what I've entrusted to him until that day.
Hold on to the pattern of sound teaching you heard from me, with the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.
Guard the precious truth entrusted to you through the Holy Spirit who lives in us.
You know that everyone in Asia turned away from me, including Phygelus and Hermogenes.
May the Lord show mercy to Onesiphorus and his household. He often refreshed me and wasn't ashamed that I was in chains.
When he came to Rome, he searched hard for me and found me.
May the Lord grant him mercy from the Lord on that day. You know how much he helped me in Ephesus.
So, my child, be strengthened by the grace that is in Christ Jesus.
Pass on to reliable people what you heard from me in front of many witnesses, so they'll be able to teach others too.
Share in suffering like a good soldier of Christ Jesus.
No soldier on duty gets tangled up in everyday affairs. They want to please the one who enlisted them.
An athlete doesn't win the prize unless they compete according to the rules.
The farmer who works hard should be the first to enjoy a share of the harvest.
Think about what I'm saying. The Lord will help you understand it all.
Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, descended from David. This is the Good News I preach,
and for it I'm suffering—even to the point of being chained like a criminal. But God's word can't be chained.
So I endure everything for the sake of God's chosen people, so they too may receive salvation in Christ Jesus and eternal glory.
This saying is trustworthy: ‘If we died with him, we'll also live with him.
If we endure, we'll also reign with him. If we disown him, he'll disown us.
If we're unfaithful, he remains faithful, because he can't deny who he is.’
Remind people of these things, and charge them before the Lord not to fight over words. It does no good and ruins those who listen.
Do your best to present yourself to God as someone approved, a worker who has no reason to be ashamed and who handles the word of truth correctly.
Avoid empty, irreverent talk, because it leads people further into godlessness.
Such talk spreads like gangrene. Hymenaeus and Philetus are examples.
They've wandered away from the truth, claiming the resurrection has already happened, and they're upsetting the faith of some.
Even so, God's firm foundation stands, marked with this seal: ‘The Lord knows those who belong to him,’ and ‘Everyone who names the Lord must turn away from evil.’
In a large house there are dishes not only of gold and silver, but also of wood and clay. Some are for special use, others for ordinary use.
Anyone who cleanses themselves from what is dishonorable will be like a special-use dish, set apart, useful to the Master, and ready for every good work.
Run from youthful passions. Pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, together with those who call on the Lord with pure hearts.
Don't get involved in foolish, ignorant arguments. You know they lead to fights.
The Lord's servant must not fight. Instead, be kind to everyone, able to teach, and patient.
Gently correct those who oppose you. God may give them a change of heart so they can know the truth.
Then they may come to their senses and escape the devil's trap, after being captured by him to do his will.
Understand this: the last days will be difficult.
People will love themselves and money. They'll brag and act arrogantly, insult God, disobey their parents, show no gratitude, and reject what is holy.
They'll have no natural affection, refuse to make peace, slander others, lack self-control, act brutally, and hate what is good.
They'll betray people, act recklessly, become conceited, and love pleasure instead of God.
They'll look religious but reject its power. Stay away from people like that.
Some of them worm their way into homes and take control of vulnerable women burdened with sins and led by all kinds of desires.
These women are always learning but never able to reach a full understanding of the truth.
Just as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, these people oppose the truth. Their minds are corrupt, and their faith is counterfeit.
But they won't get far. Their foolishness will become clear to everyone, just as it did with those two.
You have followed my teaching, way of life, purpose, faith, patience, love, and endurance.
You know about my persecutions and sufferings in Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra. I endured them all, and the Lord rescued me from them all.
In fact, everyone who wants to live a godly life in Christ Jesus will be persecuted.
But evil people and impostors will go from bad to worse, deceiving others and being deceived themselves.
But you must stay with what you learned and became convinced of, because you know who taught you.
From childhood you've known the holy Scriptures, which can make you wise for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus.
All Scripture is breathed out by God and is useful for teaching, exposing error, correcting, and training people in righteousness,
so that everyone who belongs to God may be capable and fully equipped for every good work.
I charge you before God and Christ Jesus, who will judge the living and the dead when he appears and establishes his Kingdom:
preach the word. Be ready whether the time is convenient or not. Correct, warn, and encourage with great patience and careful teaching.
A time is coming when people won't put up with sound teaching. They'll follow their own desires and surround themselves with teachers who tell them what they want to hear.
They'll turn away from the truth and chase after myths.
But you, stay clear-minded in every situation, endure hardship, do the work of an evangelist, and complete your ministry.
My life is already being poured out like an offering, and the time for my departure is near.
I've fought the good fight, finished the race, and kept the faith.
Now a crown of righteousness is waiting for me. The Lord, the righteous judge, will award it to me on that day—and not only to me, but to everyone who longs for his appearing.
Do your best to come to me soon,
because Demas abandoned me, in love with this present world, and went to Thessalonica. Crescens went to Galatia, and Titus to Dalmatia.
Only Luke is with me. Get Mark and bring him with you, because he's useful to me in the ministry.
I sent Tychicus to Ephesus.
When you come, bring the cloak I left with Carpus in Troas, along with the books—especially the parchments.
Alexander the metalworker did me a lot of harm. The Lord will repay him for what he did.
Watch out for him, because he strongly opposed our message.
At my first defense, no one stood with me. Everyone deserted me. May they not be held accountable for it.
But the Lord stood by me and gave me strength, so the message could be fully proclaimed through me and all the Gentiles could hear. I was rescued from the lion's mouth.
The Lord will rescue me from every evil attack and bring me safely into his heavenly Kingdom. To him be glory forever and ever. Amen.
Give my greetings to Prisca and Aquila, and to the household of Onesiphorus.
Erastus stayed in Corinth, and I left Trophimus sick in Miletus.
Do your best to come before winter. Eubulus sends greetings, as do Pudens, Linus, Claudia, and all the brothers and sisters.
May the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Grace be with you. Amen.
